newsitem.title: CANADA: KWG agrees to develop Cuba nickel project.
newsitem.headline: KWG agrees to develop Cuba nickel project.

text.p: KWG Resources Inc said on Thursday that it agreed with Cuban government-owned Commercial Caribbean Nickel S.A. to own jointly, develop and operate the Cupey laterite nickel mine and processing plant in Cuba.
The agreement includes the completion and operation of the Cupey project and the construction and operation of a refinery in Canada.
Total estimated cost of the projects in Cuba and Canada was US$300 million, Toronto-based KWG said.
The joint venture will be operated on a 50/50 basis, with both parties ultimately receiving 50% of Cupey's free cash flow after KWG has recovered all costs from 80% of free cash flow.
KWG has committed to arrange, over the next few months, sufficient financing to complete the Cupey project, bring it quickly into production and ensure its long term viability, the company said.
The joint venture partners are confident that the Cupey project will not be subject to any third party claims, KWG said.
The estimated US$300 million total cost of the project includes completion of the mine and processing plant, building a dedicated refinery in Canada, working capital and accrued interest.
CCN will contribute the deposit and existing processing infrastructure. The existing infrastructure plant and commercial equipment are valued at about US$600 million, KWG said.

KWG sid that in a report it commissioned as part of its due diligence inquiry, the consulting engineering firm of Watts, Griffis and McOuat (WGM) estimated that operations could begin within 18 months following a production decision and subsequent completion of financing.

The Cupey project, adjacent to a deep water port, is located 621 miles (1,000 km) southeast of Havana near the town of Moa. The Cupey plant has been nearly 100% engineered and construction is 75% complete, with certain parts up to 95%, KWG said.
Work largely slowed down on the plant, except for essential care and maintenance, when funding was exhausted during the break-up of the Soviet Union, the company said.
The WGM report concluded that "the process to be used in the Cupey plant is well proven and little difficulty should be encountered in producing nickel."
KWG said the Cupey project is designed to produce over 30,000 metric tons of nickel and 1,400 tonnes of cobalt annually for more than a 25-year period.
The defined ore reserves contain US$9.5 billion of recoverable metals at a nickel price of US$3.25/lb and a cobalt price of US$10.00/lb, KWG said.
The Cupey deposits contain 107 million tonnes of laterite and serpentine material at a grade of 1.32% Ni and 0.115% Co using a cutoff grade of 1.0% Ni, KWG said.

To date, 22 million tonnes have been classified as proven reserves and 85 million tonnes as probable reserves. In 1997, an independent Canadian engineering firm audited the methods and systems of ore resources calculations done by Geominera, a Cuban state company, KWG said.

Metallurgical tests on bulk samples taken from the sample pits demonstrated nickel and cobalt recoveries of 84-87% and 41-47%, respectively. Assuming a cobalt credit of US$10.00/lb (currently US$20.00/lb), the cash operating costs of producing nickel are forecast to be about US$1.40/lb, KWG said.

The joint-venture partners plans a further exploration program on known areas of mineralization within the Cupey property. If successful, a study will be undertaken to examine the feasibility of taking annual nickel production to over 42,000 tonnes, KWG said. ((Reuters Montreal bureau 514-985-2434))
